description:
The build gate fails on ambient build-cache state rather than on the tree it
was asked to judge, so one commit gets two verdicts depending on what the
machine happened to compile beforehand.

## Background

Two steps of `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` and `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` decide
against the environment instead of the change.

**Suite duration counts first-touch I/O.** The same merge commit, 4512 tests
passing in both runs, measured minutes apart on an idle host:

    cold:  suite-build 36,704 ms   suite-clock 43,285 ms   budget FAILED (threshold 30,000)
    warm:  suite-build    358 ms   suite-clock 22,669 ms   budget passed

`suite-build` keeps compilation outside the measured clock by design, but it
cannot pre-warm the page cache for executables written seconds earlier, so the
test step pays that I/O inside the clock. The discriminator is `suite-build`
itself: two orders of magnitude between the two runs. A reader who does not
know this signature diagnoses a real regression in the change under test, and
the correct remedy today is undocumented folklore: re-run and read the second
number.

**The incremental preflight fails on state the gate did not create.**
`incremental-preflight` (`scripts/cargo-ci.sh`) rejects a non-empty
`target/debug/incremental` before compiling anything. A rust-analyzer instance
indexing the checkout writes exactly that directory continuously, in every
worktree it has open, and it repopulates within seconds of being cleared. The
gate then reports a policy breach for a directory no gate run produced. The
standing workaround is to clear it inside a lock immediately before each run.

The two are one defect: a checker that judges the machine rather than the tree.
Both produce a red verdict that says nothing about the change, and both are
survivable only by knowing an unwritten recovery step.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Two runs of one unchanged commit reach the same budget verdict regardless of whether the build tree was already warm, so build-cache state cannot decide a gate.
- [hard] REQ-02: The suite-duration budget continues to fail a change that genuinely lengthens the suite, evidenced by a test that lengthens it and observes the failure.
- [hard] REQ-03: The incremental policy is judged by what the gate run itself produced, so incremental state written by another process before the run does not fail it.
- [hard] REQ-04: The gate-run incremental ban stays in force and stays checked; the measured rationale for disabling it during a gate run is unchanged by this work.
- [hard] REQ-05: A failure from either step names what it observed and what it compared against, so a reader can tell an environmental condition from a regression in the change.

## Notes

Scope is the checker, not the policy. `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` during a gate run
rests on a measurement — a gate compiles once and exits, so incremental state
has no later rebuild to amortize against and accumulated without bound across
runs — and it is enforced in three places: the export in `scripts/cargo-ci.sh`,
the policy-drift check in `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh`, and
`build_profile_policy_tests.rs`. The workspace manifest deliberately leaves
incremental on for ordinary interactive builds, which is unaffected. REQ-04
exists so a fix for REQ-03 does not quietly relax the ban.

The suite-duration budget is the guard that took the workspace suite from
192,994 ms to ~22,000 ms. REQ-02 exists so a fix for REQ-01 does not buy
determinism by loosening it.

Filed by the execution lead of `c639cfb5` after the cold verdict cost a cycle
on that epic's wave 15 merge. Placed under the v1.0 release container because
it is release-blocking CI correctness rather than profile work; move it if
another container owns these scripts.
title: The build gate decides on build-cache state instead of the tree
